issues.title: This disabled input element does not have an attribute that gives an accessible name to it.
issues.why_it_matters_for_persona: As a keyboard-only user who might also use a screen reader, I would encounter a disabled input field but have no information about its purpose. This is confusing because I don't know what information is being displayed or why it's not editable. It might represent a value that's been pre-filled or is conditional on another choice, and without a label, that context is lost.
remediation_instructions: Provide an accessible name for the disabled input. The method depends on whether a visible label is appropriate for the design.

If a visible label is suitable, add a `<label>` element and associate it with the input using `for` and `id` attributes. For example: `<label for='field_name'>Field Name</label><input id='field_name' disabled />`.
If the label should not be visible, use an `aria-label` attribute on the input. For example: `<input aria-label='Reason for this field' disabled />`.
expected_tool_change: An automated accessibility checker will no longer flag the disabled input for having a missing accessible name.
A screen reader will announce the input's label followed by 'dimmed' or 'disabled' when it is navigated to.
